reviewFindings.finding: Explicit retired listing status must preserve identity generations on ticker reuse
Duplicate staged candidates must not inflate publication counts or collapse distinct securities
Nonfinite adjustment ratios must fail closed
Classifier rules version must not invalidate unchanged historical artifact schema
A common first word must not certify company or SEC identity
Daily evidence budgets must rotate unprobed candidates and prevent failed symbols from starving later listings
Public reports must drop nested raw prices, provider bodies and bars arrays
Unchanged listing histories require incremental overlap refresh rather than daily full refetch
Interrupted publication must recover a demonstrably dead local lock owner without admitting concurrent writers
Search projections must retain every existing symbol and name shard reference
A subsidiary closed-end fund must not reclassify its operating parent
A first-bar action outside the observed return interval must not reject a legitimate series
Tiingo cash reinvestment must use splitFactor * (1 + divCash / exDayClose), retaining explicit prior-close semantics for generic callers

limits: Browser checks validate the existing canonical product baseline; they do not prove newly staged listings were published.
DNA split-factor and Quant computation regressions use constructed prices; actual provider history readiness is reported separately by the refresh evidence artifacts.
Publication requires QA proof bound to exact staged bytes; baseline regression results alone are insufficient.
Focused and broad suites overlap; their test counts must not be added together.
Historical provider revisions entirely before the incremental overlap may require the existing periodic long-series refresh.
